snippet.text: - Reads only of the head's tracked tree, the dependency install, Node's install, sandbox-runtime's own package, and the operating system's programs and libraries: `/bin`, `/sbin`, and `/usr`'s `bin`, `sbin`, `lib*`, `libexec` and `share`, with `/System` and `/private/var/select` on macOS and `/lib*` on Linux. Node does not start without its libraries and OpenSSL configuration, a shell needs its own, and Linux runs sandbox-runtime's seccomp helper from its package; the maintainer accepted these reads on 2026-11-07. On macOS `/usr/bin/git` is a launcher that cannot run in the sandbox, so before a probe opens the host is asked where the developer tools' git lives, and the probe may read that one git program, which a link in the probe's scratch puts on its `PATH`, git's exec path, its `share/git-core` and its system configuration. The program's neighbours in the developer tools' `usr/bin`, such as its compilers, are neither granted nor on the probe's `PATH`. Where that configuration does not exist the probe's git runs under `GIT_CONFIG_NOSYSTEM=1` instead, since the sandbox refuses the absent file's open as not permitted, which git treats as fatal; Melian's own git calls keep that variable, and no other of git's, from the caller's environment. Each but the configuration must lie inside the developer directory, and none may hold or sit inside the reviewer's home; any other answer, or a git before 2.42, leaves git unavailable to probes, and `melian doctor` says so. [The decision](decisions/2026-11-22-probes-run-git-and-workspace-imports.md) records the checks, and the reads the maintainer accepted on 2026-11-22.

trigger.snippet: | Lens request, producer `lens`, `lensRequest`, listed by `selectionOf` | `pipeline/src/lens-request.ts`, `pipeline/src/review.ts`, `pipeline/src/lens-reuse.ts` | attaches a review to its existing lens task, live or finished, when every run's request matches. Otherwise copies into the new task each lens whose earlier run had the same request and stands, as `runStands` decides: its record reads ran, on models the plan accepts, and every probe it tried ended conclusively. It copies from a task shown the same callers, a probing run included with its probe evidence and stored reruns, by [the per-request decision](../decisions/2026-11-15-lens-runs-reused-per-request.md) and [the probing reuse decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-finished-probing-runs-are-reused.md) | The review's nonce, under `nonce`. The caller section and the Enola graph its tools read, under `bestEffort`, since a host whose graph query failed would otherwise rerun every lens. The preference file's path in the standards' source, which names the host. Who set the route, and the credential, by [the run identity decision](../decisions/2026-11-08-lens-run-identity.md). The key holds the run under the fixed nonce, its route, thinking, level, budgets, instructions and prompt with the enclosing functions, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-14; the injection policy and the name of the section Pi renders it in; the installed versions of Pi Durable and pi-ai, which render the system prompt and turns and write them into each provider's request, read from each package's own `package.json`; every tool offered by name, description, schema, output limits and argument bound, and the bounds every lens tool cuts what it shows to, `lensToolLimits`; both failover wordings, `handoverWording`, the one that continues earlier work and the one that starts afresh, since a conversation's history picks between them at run time; a probing run's tools; base, head, `escalateAt` and the escalation; and the standards by text, source and trust. A lens with `standards: false` keys no standards text, only their source and trust, so turning a lens's standards off asks its runs again once, by [the decision of 2026-11-19](../decisions/2026-11-19-lenses-get-only-the-standards-they-cite.md). As a lens record's key, it lets `melian records relay` take a lens run's early copy, with no check, beside a round that reads a lens record under the same key, by [issue #397](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/397). For a run that probes, it holds the probing wording its planner and prober read: the shared lines, and the entries in core's `lensProbingWording` of its lens's `probesAs`, or of its own name. So a change to one lens's words asks no other lens's run again. [Issue #493](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/493) changed the trust-boundary lens's probing wording on purpose, so its probing runs are asked again once. For a run that escalates to another, it holds the shared lines, which carry its findings on, by rule 8 and [the per-lens wording decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-probing-wording-per-lens.md). For a run offered `list_mutants`, the key holds the instrumenter that answers it, `@stryker-mutator/instrumenter`, by [the decision of 2026-11-16](../decisions/2026-11-16-lens-request-keys-the-mutant-instrumenter.md). It holds its version, read from the `package.json` of the package the tool resolves. It holds its source, the checkout's install or Melian's, or `unavailable` when neither resolves. A run not offered the tool keys nothing more. A probing run's environment names its host by one value, `probingHost`, whose architecture and Node version come from core's `hostFacts`: the sandbox's platform and kind, the installed sandbox-runtime release, read from its own `package.json`, and the CPU architecture and version of the Node that runs the probe. Left out of that value: the operating system's release, since the platform names the system; the CPU's model, since the architecture names the instruction set Node runs; whether the filesystem folds case, since a probing run is reused only from its own checkout's store, so a temporary directory moved to a volume that folds differently copies a run probed under the other rule; and the host's locale and clock, which no probe should hang on. A probing run's environment holds the base policy's `probe.conditions` when it names any, since a condition changes which file a bare import loads, and holds nothing for an empty list, so a request asked before the key had conditions keeps its key. It leaves out where the developer tools' git lives on macOS, which names the host's install as the read paths do. Left out of the request, by [the probing reuse decision](../decisions/2026-11-16-finished-probing-runs-are-reused.md): what Melian's probe runner gives a probe and what `run_probe` returns, until [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437), so a release that changes them copies a run probed under the old code; and what the read paths hold, the installed dependencies of the code under test among them, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16, so a reinstall between two reviews of one head copies the run and its conclusive reruns. A task stored before the key, lens task version 6, holds no request key, so nothing is copied from it and the first review after the upgrade runs every lens once. The lens tools' own code, `list_mutants`'s included, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-15: the text each tool returns to the model, what each tool does, and the lens extension's code, which the key cannot hold as data. Rule 8 forbids hashing source at run time, so [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437) ties a code version to a hash of them in a test; until then a change there reuses runs asked under the old code. Chord, Pi's composition runtime, which shows a model nothing. The packages Pi Durable and pi-ai depend on, such as the AWS and Smithy packages under pi-ai's Bedrock client, by the maintainer's acceptance of 2026-11-15: they resolve through caret ranges, so a reinstall can change how a request is built while both versions stay the same, and hashing the install would ask every lens again whenever any dependency moved; [issue #470](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/470) keys only the packages that build a model request. The packages beneath the instrumenter, such as Babel, which a reinstall can move while the instrumenter's version stays the same, by the maintainer's ruling of 2026-11-16, [as recorded on pull request #492](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/pull/492#issuecomment-6907598594). The code that handles the answer, until [issue #437](https://github.com/melian-agent/melian/issues/437) |

snippet.text: An earlier run at a857d22b5 left 21 survivors, all in `probe-git.ts` and `probe.ts`. Four were checks that could never decide, so 4862d978b removed them: a developer directory of `/`, which the home check already refuses; a git that is the developer directory, which is never an executable file; an empty path in `holds`, which the rest of the expression answers; and `throwIfNoEntry: false` on a path that always exists. The coordinator accepted the removals on condition that each keeps a test: "a developer directory at the root", "a git program at the developer directory itself", "a developer directory at the reviewer's home" with "an empty answer", and `probe-git-vanish.test.ts`. The last fails on the removed check, which granted a configuration that vanished before it was checked. The rest were tests too kind to the code, and the same commit tightened them.
